name: TherapyNotes vs Valant
title: TherapyNotes vs Valant: Behavioral Health EHR Comparison (2026)
description: Compare TherapyNotes and Valant EHR for mental health practices. See differences in pricing, e-prescribing, outcome tracking, and which is best for therapists vs psychiatrists.

summary.bottom_line: TherapyNotes is ideal for therapists and counselors who want simplicity, affordability, and exceptional customer support. Valant is better suited for psychiatrists and larger behavioral health organizations that need robust e-prescribing, outcome tracking, and analytics.

sections.heading: TherapyNotes vs Valant: Overview
sections.content: TherapyNotes and Valant are both purpose-built behavioral health EHRs, but they target different segments of the mental health market. TherapyNotes is known for its simplicity, affordability, and exceptional customer support—it's the go-to platform for therapists, counselors, and social workers who prioritize ease of use. Valant is designed for psychiatrists and larger behavioral health organizations that need robust prescribing workflows, outcome tracking, and analytics capabilities.

sections.heading: e-Prescribing & Medication Management
sections.content: This is where Valant has a clear advantage for prescribers. Valant offers integrated e-prescribing with built-in PDMP (Prescription Drug Monitoring Program) lookups and EPCS (Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances). TherapyNotes offers e-prescribing as a separate add-on priced per prescriber, and users have cited concerns about cost-effectiveness. For psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners who prescribe controlled substances, Valant's integrated prescribing workflow is more streamlined.

sections.heading: Outcome Tracking & Analytics
sections.content: Valant was built with outcome measurement in mind. It offers robust analytics, configurable clinical workflows, and reporting dashboards for tracking patient progress over time. This makes it particularly valuable for larger practices that need to demonstrate treatment effectiveness or participate in value-based care arrangements. TherapyNotes offers basic outcome measures but lacks the depth of Valant's analytics suite.

sections.heading: Ease of Use & Support
sections.content: TherapyNotes wins decisively on usability and support. The interface is clean and intuitive, with well-structured note templates designed by clinicians. More importantly, TherapyNotes offers 24/7 phone and email support on all plans—a rarity in the EHR space. Valant, while powerful, has a steeper learning curve. Users report that onboarding takes time, templates are less flexible, and customer support response times can be slower.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: The choice often comes down to whether you prescribe medications:

recommendations.when: You're a therapist, counselor, or social worker who doesn't prescribe, you want 24/7 support, you prioritize ease of use, or you're running a smaller practice on a budget
You're a psychiatrist or psychiatric NP who needs integrated e-prescribing with PDMP, you want robust outcome tracking and analytics, or you're running a larger behavioral health organization
You want the best of both worlds—strong prescribing workflows AND fast documentation with the menu-driven content engine

faqs.q: Is TherapyNotes or Valant better for psychiatrists?
faqs.a: Valant is generally better for psychiatrists due to its integrated e-prescribing with PDMP lookups, EPCS support, and medication management workflows. TherapyNotes can work for prescribers but requires a separate e-prescribing add-on and isn't as streamlined for medication-focused visits.

faqs.q: Which is more affordable: TherapyNotes or Valant?
faqs.a: TherapyNotes is more affordable with transparent pricing starting at $69/month for solo practitioners and $50/month per additional clinician. Valant uses custom enterprise pricing that typically costs more, especially for smaller practices.

faqs.q: Does TherapyNotes have outcome tracking like Valant?
faqs.a: TherapyNotes offers basic outcome measures like PHQ-9 and GAD-7, but Valant has more robust analytics and reporting capabilities for tracking patient progress over time. If outcome-driven care and analytics dashboards are priorities, Valant is the stronger choice.

faqs.q: Can I switch from Valant to TherapyNotes?
faqs.a: Yes, TherapyNotes offers free data import assistance from other EMRs. Contact TherapyNotes support to coordinate the migration. Expect 2-4 weeks for a full transition, and note that you may lose some Valant-specific analytics configurations.
